correctness.rationale: Every acyclic orientation of K_{2,q} belongs to one of the two ternary product families excluding simultaneous opposed mixed column types; their binary overlap yields D=2·3^q−2^q distinct zonotope vertices. Central sign inversion gives mean zero. Leaf coordinates have zero cross-covariance and second moment (4·3^{q−1}−2^q)/D, yielding q−1 leaf-contrast eigenvalues. Counting mixed columns with binomial q,1/3 under each family gives E[(hub_A−hub_B)^2]/2=q(q+2)3^{q−2}/D. The remaining orthogonal block direction is determined by the zero-sum relation and leaf variance: λblock=(q+2)λleaf/2. These span the zero-sum hyperplane, while 1 is a null eigenvector. The sign of λblock−λhub=(q+2)/D[(6−q)3^{q−2}−2^{q−1}] is positive for q=3,4,5 and negative for q≥6. Exact displayed condition number and q²/12 follow by division. Uniformity is by distinct acyclic orientations, not by linear extensions or volume.

value.rationale: Vertex-uniform discrete inertia is a natural, distinct statistic from continuous polytope inertia and radial shell frequencies. The exact three-eigenspace tensor identifies a sharp six-leaf switch of extremal direction, one leaf later than the volume-measure switch, and quadratic worsening of condition number; it supplies an exact measure-sensitive geometry classification.

limitations: Canonical unit edge incidence realization only, q≥3 and uniform distinct vertices; not continuous volume, Gaussian normal-cone sampling or random linear extensions.
